name: Resource Management Plan
purpose: Part of the project management plan. It guides how team and physical resources are allocated, managed and released: how the type, number and skill level of people are estimated, how they are acquired, organized, trained, rewarded, developed and released, and how materials, equipment and supplies are identified, acquired and managed. It is generally developed once and does not change.

elements.guidance: Methods used to identify the skill sets and skill levels needed, including techniques to estimate how many resources: information from past projects, parametric estimates or industry standards. The blank form prints a table of Role, Number and Skill Level.
How staff will be brought on, including differences in on-boarding between internal and contract team members.

How team members will be managed and eventually released; methods may vary with the project manager's authority and with internal versus contract staff; release should include knowledge transfer. The blank form prints only the release half.
A hierarchy chart of project reporting and organization.

Per role: the role or job title with a short description; authority (decision-making, approval and influence levels such as alternative selection, conflict management, prioritizing, rewarding and penalizing); responsibility (duties, processes, hand-offs to other roles); qualifications (prerequisites, experience, licenses, seniority); competencies (specific skills and capacities, languages, technology). The blank form prints a table of Role, Responsibility and Authority.
Required training on equipment, technology or company processes, and how and when it will be done.
Reward and recognition processes and their limits.
Methods for developing individual members and the team as a whole.

Methods used to identify materials, equipment and supplies, including units of measure and techniques to estimate amounts: past projects, parametric estimates or industry standards. The blank form prints a table of Resource, Amount and Grade.
How equipment, materials and supplies are acquired: buy, lease, rent or pull from inventory; acquired resources must align with procurement management processes.
How materials, equipment and supplies are managed so they are available when needed, including inventory, supply chain and logistics.

tailoring: When outside contractors are brought in, say how to on-board them and how to give them the information they need without access to proprietary data; this may involve a non-disclosure agreement or similar forms.
Team or physical resources acquired from outside the organization must follow the organization's and the project's procurement policies.
Projects with large amounts of inventory, supplies or material should either reference organizational policies on managing physical resources or give enough detail to ensure proper control.

citation: Book of Forms form 2.26, PDF pages 115 to 117 (printed pages 104 to 106)
notes: The prose table (Table 2.24) and the blank form (PDF pages 118 to 119, printed pages 107 to 108) differ; the blank form wins. Differences: the table has Team member management, the form prints only Staff Release; the table's Qualifications and Competencies have no column on the form; the form's Number, Skill Level, Amount and Grade columns are not described separately in the table. The book names estimating techniques here (past projects, parametric estimates, industry standards) and does not describe them further. The prose gives no section on adaptive projects. The intro also says the plan covers rewards and recognition, which only get one line in the table.
